aboutWork: I studied physics and worked in data engineering. Now I work on AI and digital innovation. I like figuring out how things work and using what I learn to build something. Writing software gives me a way to explore a new problem and try out an idea.
aboutResearch: In my own time I build apps, experiment with video game mods and study geometry through Ringmin, my independent research project. I also tutor students in math and physics.
philosophy: I want to keep learning, test my ideas and make open-source tools that others can use.

geckoPageLead: A Pokédex and an assistant for the Pokémon game you’re playing.
geckoOverviewText: Prof. Gecko combines a searchable Pokémon reference with answers to questions in everyday language. The app is available in Italian and English.
geckoRagText: Before answering, the RAG assistant retrieves documents for the game version and generation you selected.
geckoToolsText: Look up a Pokémon in the Pokédex, explore the Data Hub and compare Pokémon as you put a team together in the Team Builder.
geckoAccessText: Maurizio Falconi (falker47) developed Prof. Gecko. The web app is public and its source code is private.
camaPageLead: A social deduction game for 3–12 people sharing one phone.
camaCardsText: Enter the players’ names and choose which roles to include. Take turns looking at your card in private. Civilians share a word, Moles get a similar one and the Chameleon has to bluff.
camaClueText: Each player says a word or short phrase. Give the other Civilians enough to recognise your clue while keeping the secret word from the Chameleon.
camaVoteText: Compare clues and vote on whom to eliminate. Play continues until the Civilians or the impostors win, then the game awards points.
camaOfflineText: After the first load you can play offline. Install the web app (PWA) on a compatible device or get the Android version from Google Play.

usesRouterText: With good mobile reception indoors, this router turns a data SIM into home Wi-Fi. Compare the data allowance and monthly cost with your fixed-line plan.
usesMonitorText: It fits in my backpack and gives me a second screen when I’m working away from home. On my PC the supplied USB-C cable carries both video and power.
usesChargerText: I charge several devices from one power adapter. GaN packs a lot of power into a small charger, which saves space in my bag.
usesCameraText: I get motion alerts and can speak through the camera from my phone. With enough sunlight I rarely need to recharge it. Alerts and remote control need Wi-Fi.

researchProgramSummary: Ringmin asks how small the central circle can be. The first paper certifies solutions for finite cases. The second describes what happens as the number of circles grows.
researchPaperITitle: Arranging circles of radii 1,2,…,n around a central circle: a Supnick TSP and certified finite optima
researchPaperIResult: Certified global optima for every n from 3 to 14.
researchPaperISummary: The paper reduces circle ordering to a Supnick/anti-Monge traveling salesman problem. Explicit certificates and an independent verifier let readers reproduce the results. For larger n, the candidates are heuristic.
researchPaperIITitle: Minimum central circles: an effective characterization of the global asymptotic constant
researchPaperIIResult: As n grows, R*(n) = C* n² + o(n²).
researchPaperIISummary: Finite linear programs on balanced words characterize C* with a rigorous error bound that tends to zero. Finding an elementary closed form or an efficient way to evaluate C* remains open.
